title: Intraocular Endolaser Systems: Clinical & Surgical Masterclass
summary: Endolaser photocoagulation is an indispensable surgical technique in vitreoretinal and glaucoma procedures. Delivered directly into the intraocular space via optic fiber probes, it provides precise photothermal tissue ablation, retinopexy, and ciliary ablation under direct microscopic or endoscopic visualization.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Endolaser photocoagulation refers to the intraocular administration of laser energy via a micro-fiberoptic probe inserted through a micro-incisional port (23G, 25G, or 27G) during vitreoretinal surgery or glaucoma procedures. It delivers coherent light directly to intraocular target tissues—primarily the Retinal Pigment Epithelium (RPE) for retinopexy/panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) or the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium during Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation (ECP). Unlike transpupillary indirect laser delivery, endolaser circumvents anterior segment opacities (small pupils, dense cataracts, vitreous hemorrhage) and enables precise thermal lesion placement with minimal energy dissipation.

rows: Gold standard for endophotocoagulation (PRP, retinopexy). Rapid thermal uptake, sharp lesion definition.
Preferred for Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation (ECP); penetrates sclera/ciliary stroma; lower xanthophyll absorption.
Minimal foveal xanthophyll absorption; ideal for macula-sparing retinopexy and vascular anomalies.
Sub-threshold therapy for diabetic macular edema and central serous chorioretinopathy with zero scar expansion.

branches: Curved / Angled Probes (Peripheral retinopexy without excessive scleral depression)
Flexible Steerable Probes (360° peripheral access in phakic/stiff eyes)
Illuminated Endolaser Probes (Combines light pipe + laser fiber; frees one hand)
Aspirating Endolaser Probes (Simultaneous subretinal fluid drainage & laser retinopexy)
Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation Probes (18G-20G probe with video camera, light source, 810nm diode laser)

sections.title: Step-by-Step Surgical Technique: Retinal Endophotocoagulation
content: Step 1: Trocar Placement & Media Preparation — Establish standard 23G/25G/27G pars plana vitrectomy ports. Complete core/peripheral vitrectomy and ensure adequate fluid-air or fluid-silicone medium transition.
Step 2: Aiming Beam Verification — Introduce the endolaser probe into the mid-vitreous cavity. Confirm concentric aiming beam geometry and adjust brightness to visualize tissue distance.
Step 3: Distance & Spot Titration — Position probe tip 1.0 to 2.0 mm from retinal surface. Remember: energy density varies inversely with the square of distance (closer tip = smaller, intense burn).
Step 4: Power Setting Initialization — Begin at low power (100–150 mW) with 100–200 ms duration. Increase by 20–30 mW increments until a mild gray-white burn (Grade II) is produced.
Step 5: Pattern Execution — Apply burns spaced 0.5 to 1 burn-width apart. For retinopexy, apply 2–3 rows of confluent/semi-confluent burns surrounding retinal breaks or 360° peripheral retinopexy.
Step 6: Media Adjustment & Port Closure — Re-titrate power if switching from fluid to air/gas. Inspect periphery under wide-angle viewing before trocar removal and wound closure.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Technique: Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation (ECP)
content: Step 1: Entry Approach — Create a 2.2–2.8 mm clear corneal incision (anterior approach) or pars plana vitrectomy port 3.5 mm behind limbus (posterior approach).
Step 2: Viscoelastic Inflation — Inject cohesive viscoelastic into the ciliary sulcus behind the iris to inflate the space and optimize endoscopic visualization of ciliary processes.
Step 3: Endoscope Insertion & Focus — Insert the 18G/20G ECP endoscopic probe. Focus video monitor image onto ciliary processes (viewing 4–6 processes simultaneously).
Step 4: Energy Delivery & Titration — Set 810 nm diode laser to 0.2–0.5 W continuous wave. Paint each process from anterior to posterior until ciliary process shrinks and whitens.
Step 5: Treatment Span — Treat 270° to 360° of ciliary processes. Avoid explosion/'pop' sound (indicates tissue disruption and excessive power).
Step 6: Viscoelastic Removal & Anti-Inflammatory Coverage — Thoroughly aspirate viscoelastic from anterior chamber to prevent postoperative IOP spikes; administer intracameral/topical steroids.

sections.title: Comparative Analysis: Endolaser vs Other Delivery Systems
Complications & Risk Mitigation
content: Bruch's Membrane Rupture & Choroidal Hemorrhage: Caused by excessive power density or proximity; mitigate by titrating power upward from low levels.
Laser-Induced Choroidal Neovascularization (CNV): Secondary to focal overload and Bruch's disruption; avoid intense white 'explosing' burns.
Inadvertent Foveal Photocoagulation: Prevent by placing a macula-guard instrument or maintaining constant awareness of optic nerve/fovea landmarks during peripheral sweeps.
Scleral / Trocar Port Burn: Occurs if aiming beam fires while fiber tip is retracted inside trocar cannula; always verify tip position visual contact prior to firing.
Hypotony & Phthisis Bulbi (Post-ECP): Resulting from overtreatment (>360° ablation or excessive power); restrict initial ECP treatment to 270°-300° in high-risk eyes.

sections.title: Intraoperative Red Flags & Emergency Hazards
content: RED FLAG: Acoustic 'Pop' Sound during firing indicates tissue explosion, Bruch's membrane rupture, and high risk of immediate subretinal/choroidal hemorrhage. Immediately decrease power by 50%.
RED FLAG: Firing Laser Under Air/Gas Media at Fluid Settings. Lack of thermal heat sink in gas causes severe localized retinal necrosis and macular burn.
RED FLAG: Probe Tip Touching Lens Capsule. Direct contact with crystalline lens results in instant focal cataractogenesis and capsular rupture.
RED FLAG: Unintended Photocoagulation through Decalin/PFCL Interface. Optical refractive distortion at the fluid-PFCL interface can misdirect laser energy to the fovea.

content.explanation:
B - Beam check (Confirm aiming laser prior to intraocular entry)
U - Under-power start (Always start low: 100-150 mW)
R - Distance Rules (Inverse square law: double distance = 1/4 energy density)
N - Medium Notes (Reduce power by 30-50% in air/gas media)
S - Spacing (Keep burns 0.5 to 1 spot width apart to prevent confluent scotomas)

sections.title: High-Yield Clinical Pearls
content: Inverse Square Law Dynamic: Moving the probe tip 50% closer to the retina increases laser power density by FOUR times (400%). Control spot intensity by micro-adjusting probe distance rather than constantly pressing footpedal power dials.
Fluid-Air Exchange (AFX) Dynamics: Heat dissipation is dramatically lower in air than in BSS. Always reduce laser wattage by 30–50% when switching from fluid-filled to air-filled posterior segment.

Silicone Oil Considerations: Silicone oil refracts light differently and absorbs minimal green laser energy, but requires closer probe tip positioning due to viscous drag slowing probe maneuverability.
Illuminated Probes Efficiency: Utilizing an illuminated endolaser probe frees up the surgeon's non-dominant hand for scleral depression, bimanual tissue manipulation, or membrane peeling.
ECP Endpoint Recognition: The ideal endpoint for ECP is visible shrinkage, whitening, and posterior curling of the ciliary process. If gas bubbles appear or an audible pop occurs, energy is too high.

branches: BSS / Aqueous Fluid (Standard heat dissipation; 150-250mW baseline)
Air / Gas Fill (Reduced heat sink; decrease power by 30-50%; risk of dry retinal charring)
Silicone Oil Fill (Slight refraction alteration; proximity-dependent spot sizing; maintain 1.5mm distance)
Perfluorocarbon Liquid - PFCL (Optical distortion at meniscus; avoid firing across PFCL-BSS interface edge)

sections.title: Landmark Evidence & Clinical Studies
content: ETDRS Intraoperative Application: Validated the anti-angiogenic benefits of panretinal photocoagulation patterns. Endolaser allows complete 360-degree peripheral coverage up to the ora serrata impossible with transpupillary delivery alone.

ECP Study Group Trials: Demonstrated that Endoscopic Cyclophotocoagulation (ECP) combined with phacoemulsification significantly reduced IOP and anti-glaucoma medication dependence compared to phacoemulsification alone in open-angle glaucoma.

Micro-Incisional Vitrectomy Surgery (MIVS) Endolaser Studies: Proved that 25G and 27G flexible steerable endolaser probes achieve equivalent retinopexy efficacy to 20G probes with lower entry-site astigmatism and reduced intraoperative scleral distortion.

sections.title: Postoperative Care & Long-Term Monitoring
sections.content: Postoperative management following intraocular endolaser photocoagulation includes intensive topical anti-inflammatory therapy (prednisolone acetate 1% q1h to q2h, tapered over 4–6 weeks) and cycloplegia to maintain blood-retinal barrier integrity and reduce anterior chamber inflammation. Follow-up examinations at Day 1, Week 1, Month 1, and Month 3 should evaluate retinopexy scar pigmentation/pigmentary maturation, persistent vitreous hemorrhage, IOP control (especially post-ECP), visual field loss expansion, and secondary choroidal detachment.
